subject: body
title: Skin, Hair and Nails
about: What skin does (covers and protects, sweats to cool him, heals a scrape under a scab, grows with him), keeping it clean, melanin and freckles and why every skin color is good, goosebumps, hair that keeps the head warm and grows back after a cut, eyebrows, and nails that protect fingertips and need trimming. Hygiene sits under NC 1.PCH.1.1 and 1.PCH.1.2 (how germs spread and how to stop them) and skin colors under 1.ICHR.1.2 (what makes each person special); how skin, hair and nails work is a bridge topic. Read it together: every question and choice is read aloud.
tip: Look at the back of his hand with a magnifier: pores, tiny hairs and the lines on his knuckles.

cards.q: What covers your whole body on the outside?
cards.note: Skin is your biggest organ. It keeps dirt and germs out and keeps your insides in.

cards.q: Your skin makes sweat when you are hot. What is sweat for?
cards.note: Sweat dries off your skin and carries the heat away. Every skin color sweats the same way.

cards.q: Sweat comes out through tiny holes in your skin. What are the holes called?
cards.note: Pores are too small to see without a magnifier. You have millions of them.

cards.q: A scab is a hard crust of dried blood over a scrape. What is its job?
cards.note: The scab is a lid. Under it, your skin is quietly building a brand-new layer.

cards.q: What is growing under a scab while it is on your knee?
cards.note: When the new skin is ready, the scab falls off by itself. Leave it alone until then.

cards.q: You take a bath or shower. What does the soap wash off your skin?
cards.note: Clean skin stays healthy. Wash well under your arms, behind your ears and between your toes.
Say MEL-uh-nin. More melanin makes darker skin and less makes lighter skin; every color is good, and every color needs sunscreen outside.

cards.q: Some people have little brown dots on their nose and cheeks. What are they?
cards.note: Freckles are tiny spots with extra melanin. Many people get more of them in summer.

cards.q: You feel chilly and tiny bumps pop up on your arms. What are they?
cards.note: A tiny muscle pulls each hair up straight. It happens when you are cold or get a surprise.

cards.q: What grows on top of your head and helps keep it warm?
cards.note: Hair also shades your head from the sun. A hat helps on cold days and sunny days.

cards.q: You get a haircut. What happens to your hair after that?
cards.note: Hair grows about half an inch every month. That is why haircuts keep coming.

cards.q: Does it hurt when hair is cut?
cards.note: The part of your hair you can see is not alive, so it has no feeling. Only pulling hurts.

cards.q: Eyebrows are hair too. What do eyebrows do for you?
cards.note: Eyebrows steer sweat and rain off to the side. Eyelashes catch dust before it reaches your eye.

cards.q: What are the hard covers on the tips of your fingers?
cards.note: Nails are made of the same tough stuff as hair. Toenails protect your toes the same way.
Nails also help you pick up tiny things like a bead or the edge of a sticker.

cards.q: Nails keep growing. What should a grown-up do when yours get long?
cards.note: Short, clean nails hold fewer germs. Trimming does not hurt, just like a haircut.

cards.q: You grow bigger every year. What does your skin do?
cards.note: Skin is stretchy and makes new skin all the time. Old bits flake off so tiny you never see them.
